doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Crescent Bed Factory, Joey Cola and Chinatown
summary: Allen asks about the Crescent Bed Factory, Joey Cola, Tulane Avenue's Chinatown, Chinese cookies and food.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you ever make any springs? The Crescent Bedfactor? That was mine. That place is still there. Where is that? The Crescent Bedfactor.
That's near the big hotel at Tulane and Broad? The one where the judge sends you? For free rent? From the jail, huh? I just never have been there.
Was he playing trumpet there? He was just a youngster.
Any other musicians there besides Kola? Well, Kola, that's his last name. No, Joey Cola was his name.
Oh, Sheik? I never knew his name.
He never called no George Cola or nothing.
We called him Shook.
Gray-Eyed Joey's. Yeah, yeah, yeah.
He said this when I left. I left him blowing.
Oh, yeah. I see. Well, Tulane Avenue, were you ever around Chinatown now?
Long years ago. He used to work in there with them Chinas. We used to have a little bag of cookies.
What kind of cookies?

Chinese cookies. The fortune cookies like we had last time. Yeah, you got a bag of those to clean up and wrap up the front. What about almond cookies? Did you ever have those? Never had those. I'm just curious. Could they talk English? Oh, yeah. Tell me a little bitch. You know what you want you to do? Uh-huh.
Were they any different from anybody else in their wallet?

I never had five people too different, Dick. Yeah. I mean, you have the same thing no matter where you go. Yeah. It's just a matter of staying away from the bad, which is all we do. People are all like that. Yeah. All the way down. There's no, well, great. Isn't there all good? Giving yankins? Yes. All the sudden.
All the sudden.
Yeah. They have been half. They have been doing half.
The Chinese, what about their food?
Well, they have a different way of cooking than an expression. Yes. I'm like that food. Yeah. I'm like that food. I'm like that food. I'm like that food. There you go. There you go. Too bad stuff.
Too much meat.
I like it. I stuff like stuff I think it's always been popular in New Orleans. All the musicians that I know like Chinese. Did I ask you how many languages your father spoke?
